data.body:
The concurrency group is keyed by `github.sha`, but the layer being published (`aws-durable-execution-sdk-java-otel-plugin`) is a single, fixed-name, multi-region resource, not a per-commit resource. Two runs triggered from different commits (e.g. a manual `workflow_dispatch` on `main` racing a `release` publish for an older tag, or two releases published back-to-back) get different `github.sha` values and therefore run **concurrently**, issuing overlapping `list-layer-versions` / `publish-layer-version` / `add-layer-version-permission` calls against the same layer name across ~34 regions simultaneously. This is exactly the class of problem the repo already guards against elsewhere (see `conformance-tests.yml` / `e2e-tests.yml`, which intentionally use a static `group:` with a comment explaining why concurrent runs against a shared resource must be serialized rather than deduplicated by commit). It also relies on `github.sha` accurately reflecting the released commit for `release` events, which is not guaranteed (for `release`-triggered workflows `github.sha` is documented to reflect the default branch tip at event time, not necessarily the tagged commit).

Fix: use a static group name so all publish runs against this shared layer are fully serialized, matching the existing project convention:
```yaml
concurrency:
  group: lambda-layer-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false
```
